subject: Post-call: Private VPC data flow & privacy questions (AcmeHealth)

Subject: Post-call follow-up: Private VPC data flow & privacy questions

Hi Sophie — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a list of follow-ups from our side so we can scope the Private deployment correctly:

Summary from call:
- Goal: Host inference for AcmeHealth patient-facing features in a Private deployment (VPC / customer-managed).
- Primary concerns: PII/PHI handling, data residency (US), retention & logging controls, egress restrictions, and options for on-prem/air-gapped workloads.

Open questions / asks from Acme we want to confirm:
1) Data classification: can you confirm whether the model inputs will contain PHI under HIPAA? If so, any specific subtypes (SSNs, medical notes, images)?
2) Retention: what is your required retention period for request/response logs and audit traces (default ask: 7 years for regulated records)?
3) Logging policy: do you require customer-facing content to be excluded from long-term storage, and do you need redaction/hashed transcripts?
4) Network boundaries: do you have a whitelist of egress destinations (e.g., internal telemetry endpoints, KMS, monitoring)? Will outbound egress be completely blocked for some workloads?
5) On-prem / air-gapped: are there workloads that must be fully air-gapped or available only to on-prem infrastructure? If so, what constraints (no internet, dedicated hardware, air-gap window)?

What we can commit to from Redwood (high level):
- Private (VPC) deployment with customer-managed NAT and strict egress rules.
- Ability to disable long-term content storage and retain only ephemeral audit logs if required.
- KMS/HSM integration (bring-your-own-key) for model artifacts and data-at-rest.
- Option for an on-prem installation with limited connectivity (some additional lead time and validation required).

Attached: redwood-dataflow-template.pdf — a simple template to map your data flows to help us design the network/egress rules. Please attach your internal network diagram and any compliance requirements when you can.

Next steps:
- Sophie / IT Security to share internal network diagram and retention requirements.
- Schedule 60-minute technical deep dive between Acme SWIFT security/SRE + Redwood solutions engineering (Vivek) — propose Thu 8/12 10:00am PT or Fri 8/13 11:00am PT.
- We'll prepare a deployment options doc and an initial SOW/quote after the deep dive.

Thanks — looping Vivek for the technical follow-up and Rishi for commercial next steps.

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-call follow-up: Private VPC data flow & privacy questions

Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary and template. A few notes from IT Security to help you scope: 

1) Data classification: yes — will include PHI (patient notes and identifiers). We also pass device IDs and some financial identifiers.
2) Retention: regulatory requirement is up to 7 years for audit records. For request/response content we prefer not to retain PII longer than 30 days unless explicitly logged for an active investigation.
3) Logging: we require option to disable persistent storage of input/output content. Audit logs (metadata-only) should persist for 7 years. Any content stored for debugging must be encrypted, access-controlled, and marked with retention policies.
4) Egress: most workloads must have outbound blocked. We can allow very limited egress to the following endpoints: our KMS (kms.acmehealth.internal), internal monitoring endpoints (metrics.acmehealth.internal), and the Redwood control plane IPs (to be provided).
5) On-prem / air-gapped: we have two clinical workloads that must remain air-gapped (no internet). Those will run on dedicated hardware in our data centers. We'll need an on-prem deployment option for those.

I've attached our internal network diagram and a short compliance brief.

Attachments: acmehealth-internal-network-diagram.pdf; acme-sccm-requirements.docx

We can do Thu 8/12 10:00am PT for the technical deep dive — please confirm attendees and dial-in method (we use MS Teams).

Thanks,
Sophie Barnes

Hi Sophie — thanks for the detail and the diagram, very helpful. Quick technical notes ahead of Thu's call: 

- Egress controls: Redwood Private can be deployed inside your VPC with customer-managed NAT/Gateway. Outbound egress can be restricted by security groups and route tables to the specific endpoints you list (KMS, monitoring). For fully air-gapped workloads we support an on-prem package; note that model updates and some telemetry features require a controlled sync window unless you opt for an offline model bundle.

- Data residency / storage: we support region-pinned storage (US only). For content logs we can: 1) disable persistent storage of request/response bodies by default, 2) persist only metadata (timestamps, model id, token counts) for audit, and 3) enable optional short-term debug logs (time-limited, encrypted, access-audited).

- KMS/HSM: BYOK support exists via our KMS integration layer; we can integrate with customer KMS endpoints (we'll need the endpoint and cert details). For strict HSM-only workflows we recommend an on-prem deployment with local HSM access.

- On-prem / air-gapped: our on-prem build can be deployed in an isolated network. Two caveats: (a) model refreshes require manual offline bundle operations (we provide tooling), and (b) extended support windows for air-gapped installs are subject to additional validation and lead time.

I've attached a short Redwood Private deployment options brief that outlines these modes. For Thu's call I propose attendees: Sophie (Acme IT Security), one SRE/Network engineer, Marissa (AE), Rishi (Sales), and myself (Solutions Architect). We'll join via a Redwoods-hosted Teams link unless you prefer to share your Teams invite.
